request.spec:
A bulk settle is now all-or-nothing: if any selected claim cannot be settled by the signed-in
user (any refusal the single settle would give; going to PENDING is not a refusal), none of them is
settled, every one counts as refused and nothing is written. Otherwise every selected claim is
settled in list order as before, and after the claims' own lines one line BATCH_SETTLED
batch=<batch number> count=<claims in the batch> total=<the frozen figures of those SETTLED, added
up> is written.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A bulk settle is now all-or-nothing: if any selected claim cannot be settled by the signed-in
user (any refusal the single settle would give; going to PENDING is not a refusal), none of them is
settled, every one counts as refused and nothing is written. Otherwise every selected claim is
settled in list order as before, and after the claims' own lines one line BATCH_SETTLED
batch=<batch number> count=<claims in the batch> total=<the frozen figures of those SETTLED, added
up> is written.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as

agent.result_text:
Bulk settle is now all-or-nothing. In `bin/e2e`, the main test "batch all or nothing" and "scenario 2" pass. **"Scenario 1" and "scenario 3" fail**, both at the same step on every run, and both before the test does any bulk settle.

**What changed (server only; the front end already showed the counts and batch number):**
- `claim/BulkMoveService.java`: a bulk settle now runs as one database transaction. If any selected claim is refused by the same checks a single settle uses (or isn't on the sheet), the whole thing is rolled back. That makes every claim count as refused, and no audit lines are written, because the app only writes them once a change is saved. A claim going to PENDING is not a refusal. Otherwise the claims are settled in list order and become the next batch, inside the same transaction.
- `claim/ClaimService.java`: making the batch now writes `BATCH_SETTLED sheet=… by=… batch=<n> count=<claims in the batch> total=<sum of the frozen figures of the SETTLED ones>` after the claims' own lines. PENDING claims count toward `count` but not `total`.

**Why the two scenarios fail:**
- **Scenario 1 (spec line 278)** expects the 1.00 claim to show late-entry "no". The claim is dated 2026-03-10, inside period P1, which the test soft-closes. The app's late-entry rule marks such a claim "yes", and the test's own expected audit leaves out the `LATE_ENTRY` line that rule writes.
- **Scenario 3 (spec line 791)**: adding "Ben" is refused because his contact `ben@x` is already Cam's. The person form then keeps `ben@x` filled in, and the test's helper doesn't clear that field. So adding "Ada" next submits the same contact and is refused again.

Passing them would mean changing how late entries are decided and how the person form behaves after a refusal. That's outside this change request and might break other behaviour, so I didn't touch either. Tell me if you want me to change either feature.

I added and then deleted a temporary debug spec to read the scenario 3 error. Nothing else under `e2e/` was changed.

probe.probe_text:
I read the code only and changed nothing. Section 1 lists the figures and rules, using the code's own names. Section 2 gives my assessment.

## 1. Figures and the rules that decide them

### Per claim (claim row, `features/claims/claims.ts`; server side `ClaimController.ClaimView`)

| testid | What it shows | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| `claim-amount` | `amount`, two decimals. A negative amount makes it a **correction** (`Claim.isCorrection`) | stored |
| `claim-date` | `date`; with no date given it is `Sheet.defaultClaimDate()` (the `entryDate` if set, else the sheet's `today`) | stored |
| `claim-number` | Given by `move()` when the claim is opened, via `PeriodService.nextClaimNumber(dueBy)`. If `Sheet.numbersByPeriod()` (that is, `today >= periodNumberingFrom`) it is `<period>-<n>` for the period holding the **due-by**, or `X-<n>` if none holds it. Otherwise it is the sheet-wide `nextClaimNumber`. It is kept when the claim is voided and never reused | stored |
| `claim-due` | `dueOf()` → `claimDueCents` in `core/rates.ts`, which mirrors `Dues.due` (see "Due" below) | **computed on the client** |
| `claim-due-by` | `dueBy` = `BusinessDays.dueBy(dueFrom, terms, holidays)`: the terms-th business day after the claim's date, skipping Saturdays, Sundays and sheet holidays (terms of 0 means the date itself). It is fixed when the claim is added, and edit, redate and reassign keep it. It is only worked out again by `HolidayService.add`, for claims that are not SETTLED or VOID and whose due-by is on or after the new holiday | stored |
| `claim-overdue` | `overdue()`: the claim is OPEN or PENDING, `lateFrom` < today, and it is not deferred | client |
| `claim-period` | `periodOn(periods, dueBy)`. A claim belongs to a period **by its due-by, not its date** | client |
| `claim-status` | DRAFT → OPEN → SETTLED; OPEN → PENDING → SETTLED, or back to OPEN on reject; DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING → VOID; SETTLED → VOID (`ClaimStatus.canBecome`) | stored |
| `claim-stated` | `stated`; a statement can bind a `statedDue` | stored |
| `claim-deferred`, `claim-deferred-until` | `isDeferredOn(today)`: the claim is OPEN, `deferredUntil` is set, and today is before it | client/stored |
| `claim-proofs`, `claim-batch` (`settleBatch`), `claim-split-from`, `claim-corrects`, `claim-opened-by`, `claim-reminded`, `claim-late-entry` | stored flags and fields | stored |
| `claim-log-line … due=` | `ClaimLogLine`, written by `logged()` with `dues.due(...)` as it stood at that moment | stored |

**Terms**, fixed when the claim is added (`ClaimService.terms`): the person's own `terms`, else `Sheet.termsFor(grade on the claim's date, date)`. That is the grade's own dated `terms-<grade>`, else the sheet's dated `terms` (default 14, counted in business days since migration V53).

**`lateEntry`** (`add`): the claim's date or its due-by falls in a **soft-closed** period, or the due-by it would get under the terms in force *today* falls in one. For a split, only the new due-by is checked.

### Due: `Dues.java`, duplicated in `core/rates.ts claimDueCents`
1. **Frozen:** if `settledDue` is set, that is the due.
2. Otherwise **`figure`**: the `statedDue` if `stated` and the claim is not PENDING. Otherwise **`live`**: amount × `Rate.pct`/100, scaled to 2 decimals. The rate is `RateRepository.inForce(grade on the claim's date, claim date)`: the latest from-date on or before the date (a null from-date means "always"), and it gives nothing if that rate's `to` is before the date. There is no fallback to an earlier rate. No rate gives `null`, shown as **n/a**.
3. **Rounding** (`Sheet.roundingOn`): `HALF_UP` if the date is before `policyDate`, else `HALF_EVEN`. With no policy date it compares against the sheet's **today**, so a claim's rounding can change as today moves. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects.
4. **`withLate`/`lateOn`**: applies only to OPEN or PENDING claims that are not corrections, not settled and not deferred today. `lateFrom` = due-by + the grace of the claim's grade, in force on the claim's date (`grace-<grade>`). The number of periods is `days(lateFrom → today) / 30`. Each boundary (`lateFrom` + 30·k) adds `latePctOn(boundary)` of (figure + charges so far), rounded each time, so the charge compounds. The charge is never bound by a statement.
5. **`floored`**: the result is raised to `floorOn(claim date)` (default 1.00), applied last. Corrections get no floor and no late charge.

Other variants of the due:
- **`settling`**: the stated figure or the live figure, plus the late charge and floor, frozen at settle.
- **`approving`**: the live figure (ignoring any statement) plus late charge and floor.
- **`resettling`**: the live figure as if the claim were OPEN today, with `lateOn` and floor.

### Which claims count
- `ClaimStatus.counts()` is true for OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED.
- **`Person.countsLive`**, mirrored as `countsLive` in `people.ts`: the claim must count and must not be deferred today. An OPEN or PENDING claim that is **not stated** is also left out if `leavesLive`, meaning it is dated within any **hold** (`Hold.covers`, inclusive, open-ended allowed) or the person is **retired** (`today >= retiredFrom`).
- A statement's binding therefore keeps a held or retired person's claim counting.

### Per person (`people.ts` on the client; `Rollups.take` on the server, which is only used for audit lines)

| testid | Rule |
|---|---|
| `person-grade` | `gradeOn(today)`. Grades are dated (`gradesFrom`) and the first grade applies from the beginning of time |
| `person-claimed` | Sum of `amount` over the countsLive claims, including PENDING and negative corrections |
| `person-due-total` | Sum of the dues of the countsLive claims, **capped** at `Sheet.getCap()` (the cap in force today). It is **n/a** if the grade in force today has no rate today *and* none of the claims has a figure |
| `person-excess` | The sum before the cap minus the cap, else 0.00 |
| `person-settled-total` / `person-open-total` | Dues of the counting SETTLED / OPEN+PENDING claims. Neither is capped |
| `person-overdue-count` / `-total` | Counting claims that are `overdue` (grace-aware), and the sum of their dues |
| `person-aged-0-30/31-60/61` | Counting OPEN or PENDING dues, bucketed by days from the claim's date to today. Future-dated claims go in 0–30 |
| `person-active` | Has a counting OPEN or PENDING claim dated within [today−29, today] |
| `person-backing` | Sum of `settledDue` over the patrons' SETTLED claims dated within [today−89, today]. This does **not** apply countsLive |
| `person-period-<name>-due-total` | If the period is closed or soft-closed: the stored `personTotals` (0 for a person added since). If it is open: computed live by `countsInPeriod` (below) |
| `person-statement-count`, `person-stated-total` (n/a or blank), `person-statement-date` | stored on `Person` |
| `person-retired(-from)`, `person-hold`, holds | stored |

### Sheet totals (`rollup-*`) and the summary
- **`rollup-claimed-total`** is a plain sum.
- **`rollup-due-total`** and **`rollup-overdue-total`** are **trimmed** (`trimmedCents` / `Rollups.trimmed`): when there are three or more figures, the single highest and single lowest are dropped. People shown as n/a are skipped for the due total.
- **`rollup-overdue-count`** is a count across all people.
- **`rollup-settled-total`** and **`rollup-open-total`** are untrimmed sums.
- **Summary:**
  - `summary-grade-X-count/-active/-due-total`: people who are not retired and have that grade today; the due-total adds their capped due-totals, skipping n/a.
  - Period due-totals.
  - Counts per status.
  - Counts of voided claims per void reason.
  - Tag totals: one per tag ever used (`tagsUsed`), adding the dues of counting claims that *currently* carry the tag.
  - Month totals: one per month any claim is dated in, adding the dues of counting claims.
- **`period-due-total`**: the fixed `closedTotal` (the sum of `personTotals`) if the period is fixed, else the live sum.

### Periods (`PeriodService`, `Period`)
- **What a period's figure includes** (`totals`, and on the client `countsInPeriod`): claims whose **due-by** is in the period, judged by `statusAt(period.to)` from the status log, which must be one that counts. Claims deferred today, and OPEN/PENDING held or retired claims that are not stated, are left out. Each claim adds its due *as computed now*, including today's late charge.
- **close**: fixes `personTotals` and `closedTotal`. It is refused if the period is already closed or if the permission matrix (`close`) does not allow it. A soft-closed period can be closed, which recomputes its figures.
- **softClose**: fixes the figures the same way, but its claims stay changeable, and new claims landing in it are late entries.
- **reopen**: needs the `reopen` permission (steward by default). It clears the fixed totals.
- **Auto-close** (`todayChanged`): when the sheet's today changes and `graceDays` is set, every period that is not fixed and whose `to + graceDays < today` closes, audited with `auto=yes`. Soft-closed periods are left alone.
- **`refuseIfClosed(dueBy)`**: a claim whose due-by is in a **closed** period is refused for:
  - add (on the computed due-by)
  - edit and lock (on its due-by, and on the new date's due-by)
  - every move, approve, reject, resettle, defer, reassign and redate
  - split (checking both claims)

  It is **not** checked for proof, comment or remind.

### Status moves and who may do what (`ClaimService`, `RoleService`, `Sheet.permits`)
- **Role** (`roleOf`): **steward** if a `Delegation` covers today (the latest one wins), else the stored role, else **clerk**. `DelegationGuard` adds "acting for" to the audit.
- **Permission matrix** (`STANDING_PERMISSIONS`, overridable per sheet):
  - open, settle, void, close: clerk and steward
  - reassign, reopen: steward only
- **Hard-coded steward-only actions:**
  - approve and reject
  - resettle and redate
  - voiding a SETTLED claim, only while `today <= settledOn + VOID_SETTLED_DAYS (7)`
  - cancelling a statement
  - archiving
  - delegating (the user must be a steward in their own right; a delegation doesn't count)
- **Viewer:** `ViewerGuard` refuses every write. Bulk open, bulk settle and bulk grade let the request through and refuse each item.
- **Archived:** `ArchiveGuard` refuses everything. **As-of:** while an as-of date is being shown, `AsOfGuard` refuses every write.
- **Open:** refused if the note is blank and the due is above `noteThresholdOn(claim date)`. n/a always passes.
- **Settle:**
  - Refused if the claim is deferred today.
  - Refused if the user `isOpenedOrEditedBy` the claim (the same applies to approve).
  - Refused if `proofs == 0` and the settling due is above `proofThresholdFor(grade, date)` (the grade's own dated threshold, else the sheet's). This check runs **before** the clerk-limit check.
  - If the user is a **clerk** and the due is above the `clerkLimit` in force today, the claim goes **PENDING** instead and nothing is frozen.
- **Edit:** only a DRAFT claim, not locked by another user's editor. The due-by is kept even if the date changes. Changing today releases every lock.
- **Defer:** only OPEN, and only to a date after today.
- **Split:** only OPEN and not deferred, with 0 < amount < the claim's amount. Both claims lose their binding, and the new claim gets fresh terms and due-by.
- **Reassign:** DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING only. It unbinds the claim. Refused if the new person is retired before the claim's date, or for a correction that names no SETTLED claim of the new person.
- **Redate:** OPEN or PENDING only. It keeps the due-by, number and binding.
- **Remind:** OPEN or PENDING, once per today.
- **Proof:** refused for SETTLED or VOID.
- **Void:** needs a reason from the list whenever the list is not empty.
- **Retirement:** a claim cannot be dated after `retiredFrom` (on add, edit, redate or reassign).
- **Correction:** must name, by number, a SETTLED claim of the same person; a claim that is not a correction must name none.
- **`ref`:** unique per sheet, compared case-insensitively.

### Statements (`StatementService`)
- **take**, as of today or an earlier `asOf`:
  - An earlier date uses the snapshot from `SheetHistory`. A date after today, or before the person or sheet existed in a snapshot, is refused.
  - Each claim that `countsLive` that day is bound to its `figure`: the rate figure only, without late charge or floor.
  - Every other claim of the person is **unbound**.
  - The total is the sum of the full dues, under the same n/a rule, capped.
- **cancel** (steward only): unbinds **all** of the person's claims (an earlier binding is not restored) and shows the previous statement again.

### Imports and bulk actions
- **Paste** (`PasteService`):
  - Each line is `name,amount,date,note`; a trailing ` #ref` becomes the claim's reference.
  - Each line becomes a DRAFT claim through `ClaimService.add`, so every add rule applies.
  - It is all or nothing, with at most 1000 lines.
  - It never sets `corrects`, so a negative amount is always refused. Tags aren't supported.
- **Quick-add:** creates the person with grade **A** if they don't exist, then adds a DRAFT claim. It is one transaction.
- **Bulk moves:**
  - Order: people in the order they were added, then each person's claims by date descending, then id descending. Numbers are given out in this order.
  - Bulk **settle** is all or nothing and gets a `settleBatch` number.
  - Bulk open and bulk reassign go claim by claim.
- **Bulk grade:** edits each person separately; a viewer changes nobody.

### Dated settings (`Sheet.valueOn`)
- Settings with a from-date: clerk limit, cap, floor, terms, `terms-<g>`, late percent, `grace-<g>`, proof threshold, `proof-threshold-<g>`, note threshold. Each takes its value from the latest from-date on or before the date asked about.
- Which date each one is read at:
  - claim's date: floor, terms, grace, proof and note thresholds
  - boundary date: late percent
  - today: cap and clerk limit
- `policyDate`, `periodNumberingFrom`, `graceDays` and `entryDate` are plain values with no history.
- Grades are dated per person.
- Moving the sheet's today snapshots everything and audits SNAPSHOT lines.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

It's scattered and tangled. The core due formula is cleanly in `Dues.java`, but the rules for "what counts" and the totals are implemented several times:
- `Person.countsLive`, `Rollups`, `PeriodService.totals` and `StatementService` on the server;
- again in TypeScript (`claimDueCents`, `countsLive`, `countsInPeriod`, `trimmedCents`, `rateOn`, `gradeOn`, `valueOn`, `roundsHalfUp`) in `core/*.ts` and the 1,400-line `people.ts`, which is what actually puts the numbers on screen.

Permission and refusal rules are spread across `ClaimService` (an 800-line file), interceptors, the permission matrix and client-side pre-checks. A new developer would have to cross-check both sides, and the stale comments don't help: `Sheet.terms` still says "plus this many days", and `pending()` mentions "its date" but checks the due-by.

Two things I noticed but didn't dig into:
- Setting roles and settings has no role check beyond the viewer guard, so a clerk appears able to make themselves a steward.
- Adding a holiday can move a claim's due-by across a closed period's boundary.
